_disclaimer: SIMULATED DEMONSTRATION DATA. Fictional, procedurally generated for the BAYOU-NOVA proof of concept (2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge). Not real crew data. Not a medical record. Not for clinical use.
evaluation_note: Phase 5: Layer 1 and Layer 2 results are no longer stored here. They are computed live by lib/detection.ts from readings.json, checkins.json and anything added during the demo session, using the rules in shared/detection-rules.json. This file keeps only narrative context.

expected_adaptation_context.basis: Group-level published observations only (see shared/sources.json). Sleep: ISS crew commonly obtain less sleep in flight (barger2014_sleep). Heart rate and blood pressure: a study of six ISS astronauts found no in-flight change from preflight at rest (hughson2012_cv), so a sustained rise is not assumed to be expected adaptation. Individual expected ranges are not established.
expected_adaptation_context.summary: In-flight sleep is a little shorter than preflight, which is directionally consistent with group-level observations. Resting heart rate and blood pressure are shown beside the preflight baseline without assuming any change is expected.

uncertainty_statement: Wearable-derived and self-reported indicators carry uncertainty. Nothing here measures bone density or immune function.
